question: The European Chemicals Agency has proposed that the use of lead ammunition may continue at gunshot shooting ranges if they are able annually to collect at least 90 % of discharged lead pellets, and at rifle shooting ranges if they are equipped with bullet traps or sand traps, as defined by best practice. 1.

What is the Commission’s view on whether the lead in ammunition discharged at shooting ranges – such as shotgun pellets and rifle bullets – that is left to accumulate after it has served its intended purpose constitutes a scrap metal for the purposes of the Regulation on the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals?
If this lead does not constitute a scrap metal, can the Commission clarify the manner in which its status is defined?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.4.2024) The Regulation on the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals, REACH1, does not include a definition of ‘scrap metal’. Discarded lead ammunition may be considered waste to the extent it fulfils the definition of waste2 laid down in the EU waste legislation3.

Regulating the placing on the market or use of a substance to avoid risks to human health or the environment that might arise once the substance is at waste stage is possible under REACH and in line with the REACH objectives, as confirmed by recent EU case law4.
1 Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 18 December 2006

concerning the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH). OJ L 396 30.12.2006, p. 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A02006R1907-20231201 2 ‘Waste’ means any substance or object which the holder discards or intends or is required to discard (Article 3(1) of Directive 2008/98/EC).

3 Directive 2008/98/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 November 2008 on waste. OJ L 312, 22.11.2008, p. 3. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A02008L009820180705 4 Judgment of the General Court of 30 June 2021 in Case T-226/18 Global Silicones Council and Others v Commission.
